narrative.overview:
Your old leads are a street of dark houses at night. While the office is shut, a few windows light flat green as conversations start, and a porch light turns moonlight yellow for every booked appointment. The page walks that one night from dusk to morning: the sleeping street in the hero, one lead coming back in a real text thread, how a night runs, the consent rules, and at the end the same street at dawn with the lights out, the booked porches still on, and a calendar of bookings beside the audit form.

The world is calm, dark and generous with space. Houses are crisp flat geometry (rectangles, triangles, one small circle for a porch light) in near-black silhouette against a midnight-blue page. Light is flat colour, never a bloom: a window is either off or on. A light, wide, mid-century display face carries the headlines like painted house numbers; a sturdy grotesk does all the reading. Sections are full-width bands separated by tone or a single hairline, not cards in a row.

This world replaces the earlier "Night Shift" neon robot-crew system entirely. No robot characters, no neon glow, no phone-mockup split hero; the AI stays in the background and the visible outcome is an appointment.
keyCharacteristics: Midnight-blue tonal bands (four night steps) with hairline rules; no cards-in-a-row.
Flat silhouette houses as the recurring motif: street in the hero, same street at dawn at the close.
Green means a lit window: a live conversation, and the one primary action.
Moonlight yellow means a booked appointment, and the moon. Nothing else.
Josefin Sans Light display over Schibsted Grotesk body.
Motion happens once: windows light on load, the thread plays once if unseen; reduced motion shows the final state.

rules.name: The Two Lights Rule
rules.body: Green is a lit window: a live conversation, or the one thing to press. Moonlight yellow is a booking or the moon. If something is neither, it stays ink on night.

rules.name: The Flat Light Rule
rules.body: Windows, porch lights and buttons are flat fills. No glow, bloom, neon text-shadow or outer halo on any light. The only soft light in the system is the dawn horizon.

rules.name: The Same Street Rule
rules.body: The palette never adds a third accent. New states are expressed with the existing lights (on/off, green/yellow) or with ink weight.

rules.name: The Light Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type is Josefin Sans at weight 300 and sentence case. Never bold it, never uppercase it, never track it out.

rules.name: The Proportional Time Rule
rules.body: Times ("8:55 PM", "Thu 10:30") stay in proportional figures; Schibsted's tabular set spaces the colon awkwardly.

rules.name: The Tone-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by night step and hairline. A drop shadow appears once, on the closing form against the dawn.

dos: **Do** keep green for lit windows, live conversations and the primary action, and Moonlight Yellow for bookings and the moon only.
**Do** draw new illustration as flat silhouette geometry in Deep Night with flat lit or unlit windows.
**Do** set headlines in Josefin Sans 300, sentence case, and everything else in Schibsted Grotesk.
**Do** separate sections with night tone steps and Night Rule hairlines.
**Do** play any motion once and make sure the final state is the default HTML, visible without script and under reduced motion.
**Do** label example names, times and conversations as illustrative, once and quietly.
**Do** use the green 2px outline, offset 3px, for every focus state.
donts: **Don't** add glow, bloom, neon or text-shadow halos to green or yellow; light is flat.
**Don't** use Moonlight Yellow for warnings, highlights, decoration or general emphasis.
**Don't** bring back the robot crew, cartoon characters or the Oxanium display face from the old system.
**Don't** build rows of cards or a split hero with a phone mockup.
**Don't** loop animations or replay them on scroll.
